parameters.content:
📘 WORKFLOW DETAILS

Golf Course Turf Ops – Per-Zone Irrigation Scheduler & Pesticide REI Compliance

VALUE PROP: Fans out a course-wide sensor batch into one agronomic decision per zone — blending soil moisture, ET-adjusted water need, and pesticide-label restricted-entry-interval/buffer rules — then fans back in to push one optimized irrigation schedule to the controller and alert the crew to any compliance-restricted zones.

WHO / PROBLEM: A golf course superintendent has to balance water conservation, turf health, and pesticide-applicator regulations (label REI, water-hazard buffers) across dozens of zones every morning. Doing this by hand per zone doesn't scale past a handful of holes, and a missed REI/buffer check is a real regulatory exposure.

WALKTHROUGH:
1. Sensor gateway posts the morning batch of zone readings via webhook.
2. Today's weather (ET0, rain probability) is fetched once for the whole course.
3. Split Out explodes the batch into per-zone items (Pattern B fan-out).
4. Each zone's moisture deficit and ET-adjusted need are computed (Code).
5. Recently-sprayed zones go through AI label extraction + a real REI/buffer Code check; others skip straight through.
6. Restricted zones get zero irrigation minutes; others get a computed runtime.
7. Merge → Aggregate fan the zones back into one schedule (Pattern B fan-in), which is pushed to the controller and, if any zone was restricted, alerts the grounds crew.

NODE SUMMARY: Webhook, HTTP Request (x2), Split Out, Code (x3), If (x3), Information Extractor + Chat Model, Merge (x2), Set (x2), Aggregate, Telegram.

EXPECTED I/O: In: webhook POST of {course_lat, course_lon, zones:[...]}. Out: irrigation schedule pushed to the controller API + optional Telegram compliance alert.

STICKY COLOUR LEGEND: 1 trigger (blue) · 2 transform (grey) · 3 AI (purple) · 4 branch (yellow) · 5 storage (green) · 6 notify (red).

⚙ SETUP GUIDE

1. Import this JSON via n8n → Workflows → Import from File.
2. Create credential "Swapnil AI Labs – OpenAI" (OpenAI API) on: GPT-4o-mini for Label Extraction.
3. Create credential "Irrigation Controller API Key" (Header Auth) on: Push Schedule to Irrigation Controller.
4. Create credential "Golf Ops – Telegram Bot" (Telegram API) on: Alert Grounds Crew – Restricted Zones.
5. Set your real irrigation-controller base URL in Push Schedule to Irrigation Controller.
6. Set GROUNDS_CREW_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID to your real Telegram group chat ID.
7. Point the sensor gateway's webhook at this workflow's production webhook URL for Receive Zone Sensor Batch.
8. Adjust target moisture % and crop coefficients in Compute Soil Moisture Deficit for your grass species/climate.
9. Confirm your state's pesticide label REI defaults are reflected in the extractor's system prompt.
10. TEST: POST a sample payload with 2-3 zones (one recently sprayed) to the webhook and confirm the schedule + any alert.

EST. SETUP TIME: 30–40 minutes.

🎨 CUSTOMISATION

1. Compute Soil Moisture Deficit (Code): tune target VWC % and crop coefficients per grass type (bentgrass vs bermuda).
2. Extract REI & Buffer Requirements (Information Extractor): feed it your actual product label database instead of a text snippet.
3. Build Irrigation Controller Payload (Code): change the zone priority order (e.g. tee boxes before rough) to match your maintenance plan.
4. Alert Grounds Crew – Restricted Zones (Telegram): swap for a Slack channel post if your crew doesn't use Telegram.
5. Fetch Today's Weather Forecast (HTTP Request): swap Open-Meteo for a paid hyperlocal weather API if you need on-site station accuracy.

ℹ ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

ERROR HANDLING: External-call nodes (HTTP Request x2, OpenAI chat model, Telegram) use onError=continueRegularOutput with retryOnFail, maxTries=3, waitBetweenTries=2000ms. Code, Set, If, Merge, Aggregate, Split Out and Webhook are excluded — no independent third-party API call.

API COST / RATE LIMITS: Open-Meteo forecast is free/no-key; one OpenAI extraction call only fires for zones sprayed in the last 5 days, keeping cost proportional to actual pesticide activity, not total zone count.

DATA PRIVACY: No personal data processed — only agronomic sensor and pesticide-application data. No special handling required beyond normal operational-records retention.

N8N VERSION BUILT AGAINST: n8n 1.6x (nodes-base ~ Sept 2026), typeVersions as declared per node.

KNOWN LIMITATIONS: Offline hand-authored build, not tested against a live n8n instance. Confirm the Webhook production URL and irrigation-controller payload shape against your actual controller vendor's API on first import.

CREATOR: Swapnil AI Labs — swapnil.mandloi7@gmail.com — swapnilailabs.netlify.app

**Receive Zone Sensor Batch**
Irrigation-controller sensor gateway POSTs every zone's soil-moisture/ET reading each morning.
Method: POST /golf-zone-sensor-batch.
One payload, dozens of greens/fairways/rough zones inside it.

**Fetch Today's Weather Forecast**
Pulls hourly temp, rain probability and reference evapotranspiration (ET0) for the course.
Source: Open-Meteo forecast API.
Irrigation minutes are meaningless without knowing if rain is coming.

nodes.name: Note: Split Zones Into Individual Items

parameters.content:
**Split Zones Into Individual Items**
Explodes the sensor batch into one item per green/fairway/rough zone.
Field: zones.
Each zone needs its own moisture, REI and irrigation decision.

**Compute Soil Moisture Deficit**
Blends live soil-moisture readings with ET0 and crop coefficient per zone type.
Targets: green 28%, fairway 22%, rough 16% VWC.
The core agronomic math the whole schedule is built on.

**Recent Pesticide Application?**
Branch point 1: only zones treated in the last 5 days need a label re-entry-interval (REI) check.
Condition: days_since_pesticide_app <= 5.
Most zones on any given day were not just sprayed.

**GPT-4o-mini for Label Extraction**
Chat model backing the pesticide-label information extractor.
Model: gpt-4o-mini, temp 0.
Label language is legally exact — no room for creative rewording.

**Extract REI & Buffer Requirements**
Pulls the restricted-entry-interval hours and water-hazard buffer distance out of the product label text.
Output: rei_hours, buffer_ft, buffer_violated.
Turns unstructured label text into numbers the Code node can act on.

**Determine Zone Still Restricted**
Compares elapsed hours against the extracted REI, and checks the buffer-zone flag.
Restricted if hours_since < rei_hours OR buffer_violated.
A buffer violation blocks irrigation near the hazard regardless of REI expiry.

**Merge Restricted-Check Branch**
Recombines zones that skipped the label check (no recent pesticide) with zones that went through it.
Mode: append, 2 inputs.
Every zone reaches the irrigation decision with a consistent 'restricted' field.

**Is Zone Restricted?**
Branch point 2: restricted zones get skipped from today's irrigation run entirely.
Condition: restricted == true.
Irrigating (or letting crew onto) a zone still inside REI is a compliance violation.

**Flag Zone Skip Irrigation**
Zeroes irrigation for restricted zones and records why.
irrigation_minutes=0, skip_reason set.
Makes the compliance exception visible in the final schedule and alert.

**Compute Irrigation Run Minutes**
Converts moisture deficit + ET need into head-run minutes, unless rain makes it pointless.
Formula: deficit*1.8 + ET-need*2.2 minutes.
The actual runtime number the irrigation controller will execute.

**Merge Zone Decision Branch**
Recombines skipped and scheduled zones into one stream before aggregation.
Mode: append, 2 inputs.
Fan-in step of the Split Out → per-zone logic → fan-in pattern.

nodes.name: Note: Aggregate All Zones Into Schedule

parameters.content:
**Aggregate All Zones Into Schedule**
Collapses every processed zone back into a single course-wide schedule payload.
Field: zones[].
Closes the fan-out/fan-in loop before building the controller command.

**Build Irrigation Controller Payload**
Sorts zones by priority (greens first), sums the day's total water budget, lists every exception.
Output: schedule[], total_irrigation_minutes, exceptions[].
The exact command the irrigation controller needs to run.

nodes.name: Note: Push Schedule to Irrigation Controller

parameters.content:
**Push Schedule to Irrigation Controller**
Sends the final per-zone schedule to the physical controller that actually opens the valves.
Endpoint: POST /api/schedule.
This is the primary storage/action sink — the system of record is the controller itself.

**Any Restricted Zones Flagged?**
Branch point 3: only alerts the crew when at least one zone was skipped for compliance reasons.
Condition: exception_count > 0.
A clean run with zero exceptions shouldn't page anyone.

nodes.name: Note: Alert Grounds Crew – Restricted Zones

parameters.content:
**Alert Grounds Crew – Restricted Zones**
Pushes a same-morning alert so crew know exactly which zones to stay off / not irrigate.
Chat: grounds crew Telegram group.
Stops a crew member from accidentally entering an REI-restricted green.
